rationale: bugs_open/450, the SUPPLY half. The door half (587666be8, PBP-053, council APPROVED corr 2b236e83) stops a tool page with no tool being FILLED with prose. This stops such a page being PLANNED at all. The two are independent: neither depends on the other having landed, and either alone is an improvement. THE DEFECT: the site planner names tool pages (page_type='tool') with generic sections before their tools exist, because tools arrive from the ~3h design rotation hours-to-days later and under names the planner never saw — seotools.co.uk, 0 of 7 planned names matched what tool-deployer eventually built. The page row is minted at plan time by sync_pages, hub and nav pages link it, and generic producers fill it. THE ARMING LICENCE, and the reason this could not have been built two days ago: the 444 session's CONTRIB in bugs_open/450 objected that the order-safety property making ITS listing gate safe does NOT transfer — a listing hub's children are IN the plan, so post-plan builders cannot false-positive, whereas a tool page's producer arrives from OUTSIDE the plan, later, by design. 'Hold if no tool exists' would therefore hold every tool page on every fresh build, and whether that STARVES the tool rotation or merely removes dead rows was an explicitly open question (§7, then [UNVERIFIED]). It was answered at the rows on 2026-09-03: tool-deployer CREATES ITS OWN page rows (create_tool_component_action.go bare INSERT / UpsertPageForRole arm), its names are disjoint from the planner's, and nothing reads planned tool pages to decide what to build. The held page was never the producer's input, so holding it starves nothing — the planner's tool stubs are pure liability. That measurement is this gate's whole licence to exist, and it is stated in the code as the thing to check if the gate ever misbehaves. SHAPE, per the 444 session's own request: a SIBLING key `enforce_tool_sources` (default OFF) in a NEW file, with ZERO edits to listing_item_sources.go, so a tool-arm misfire is switchable without losing the live listing gate and their gate is revertible independently in code as well as by key. RFC_022 posture: opt-in, unsafe side default OFF, zero live consumers until the migration names it — council-gate scope, not architecture-RFC, the same judgement 444's own PLAN recorded for the sibling.

plan.summary: A planned page with page_type='tool' is held out of the plan unless a live component_level='tool' component exists on THIS site under one of the page's candidate function names (its sections, its own name, or 'tool-'+name — mirroring the tool pipeline's naming contract). Held pages file a deferred capability_gap through the shared work-item writer, on the SAME item_key builderForPageType's unavailable-builder arm already uses so the two co-dedup, plus a durable TOOL_PAGE_HELD_NO_TOOL_SOURCE finding. Realised pages are never dropped (preserve guard) but still get the receipt. Fails OPEN on infrastructure (nil DB, unparseable site id, census error) and CLOSED on a positive answer (an empty tool set means the site owns no tools). Runs BEFORE the listing gate so a /tools/ hub whose children were just held is itself held rather than shipped empty.

edits.symbol: ResolveToolItemSource / enforceToolItemSources / siteToolFunctions / toolFunctionCandidates / fileToolCapabilityGap / toolDropFindings
edits.rationale: A SIBLING of listing_item_sources.go, not a widening of it — the 444 session asked for exactly this in its CONTRIB, for independent rollback and because a tool page is not semantically a listing page. It reuses that gate's FRAME (preserve-guard rule, fail-open posture, the capability_gap shape through the shared insertWorkItem door, durable drop findings via LogActionFindings) and the package's plan-page primitives (planPageView, pageViewFromMap, droppedSectionName, warnUnrecordedDrops) while keeping its own resolver vocabulary. listing_item_sources.go is not edited at all. The resolver is PURE (the tool set is read once per plan and passed in) so it costs one query per plan rather than one per page and the whole decision is testable without a database. The census predicate is deliberately create_tool_component's OWN 'does this site already have this tool' predicate — the two must agree about what 'the site has this tool' means, or the gate holds pages the tool pipeline believes it has already built. A LIBRARY tool not deployed to this site does not count: §7 proved nothing consumes planned tool pages, so a page kept on a library match is a page nothing will ever fill.

Eight lines, immediately ABOVE the existing enforce_listing_sources block. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE ONE GENUINELY NEW DESIGN POINT IN THIS SUBMISSION: held tool children make a /tools/ hub resolve zero children, so the listing gate below then holds the hub too and no phantom /tools/ URL is planned at all. The reverse order plans an empty hub — a 444-class page — out of a plan whose tool pages were just removed. This does not contradict the listing gate's own TestResolveListing_SectionIndex_PlanChildren (planned-but-unbuilt children still count): they count when they SURVIVE validation, and these did not. Self-healing: when the rotation builds real tools, the next replan sees them in the realised set and the hub returns.

The held and kept fixtures differ in ONE fact — the site's tool set — with the same page role and plan structure, so a test cannot pass by accident of page shape. Three arms proved by mutation, each killing a DIFFERENT set: (1) resolver always-producible kills the five Held/receipt tests and no Kept test; (2) removing the page-name candidate arms kills exactly the three name-based tests and leaves the section-name and Held tests green — the arms are independently covered; (3) turning the census fail-open into fail-closed kills only CensusErrorFailsOpen, which is the arm that would otherwise starve every fresh build on a transient DB error. TestResolveTool_NearMissDoesNotResolve is the control that stops the central Held test passing for the wrong reason: the site DOES own a tool, just not this one (robots-txt-TESTER planned vs robots-txt-GENERATOR built is the bug's actual mechanism), so any fuzzy or substring match would reopen it. Two lockstep tests pin the external contracts this gate borrows: toolProducerSlug against builderForPageType("tool"), and toolFunctionCandidates against sanitiseFunction's real output.

grounded_in: bugs_open/450 §7, ANSWERED at the rows 2026-09-03 — the arming licence for this gate: 'tool-deployer CREATED its own page rows under its own names ... and the planner's names and the suggester's names are DISJOINT: 0 of 7 planned pages matched (robots-txt-tester planned, robots-txt-generator built). Consequences: (a) holding planner tool stubs starves nothing — the producer makes its own rows (the 444 CONTRIB's deadlock branch is refuted, its door-closing point stands); (b) the planner's tool pages are pure liability — no producer ever fills them.'

bugs_open/450 CONTRIB from the 444 fixing session, §2, which this submission follows: 'If extended: a SIBLING key, not an overload. The registry structure, capability_gap shape, preserve-guard rule and fail-open policy in listing_item_sources.go all transfer (it was built to take another arm) — but arm it behind its own optional key (e.g. enforce_tool_sources, default OFF) rather than widening what enforce_listing_sources means: independent rollback (a tool-arm misfire must be switchable without losing the live listing gate), and a tool page is not semantically a listing page.'

bugs_open/450 §7 on the sectionless fork, the evidence for holding EMPTY-sectioned tool pages too: 'its planned tool-channel-prioritiser had NO site_plan_sections, so the link repair's builder parked all 7 unbuilt_internal_link items at mark_no_ready_sections (HITL) instead of writing a shell, and a needs_content_page ("0 component rows — build it") joined them at 04:01Z.' — i.e. 'no shell' is a recurring human-queue tax plus a live phantom-link source, not a harmless outcome.

create_tool_component_action.go, the naming contract the candidate list mirrors: sanitiseFunction guarantees the `tool-` prefix on every function; the page is created with pages.name == cc.function ('the canonical name equals function and the acceptance coupling holds'); and the site-scoped existence probe is `cc.function = $1 AND cc.component_level='tool' AND p.site_id = $2 AND cc.is_active` — the same predicate siteToolFunctions uses, so the gate and the tool writer cannot disagree about what 'this site has this tool' means.

deploy_tool_action.go: resolveToolPageIdentity looks for an existing page named `<function>` or `tool-<function>` only — no join to the plan, no fuzzy match — which is why the candidate list carries both spellings and why a near-miss must NOT resolve.

listing_item_sources.go:19-22, the fail-open policy this arm deliberately narrows: 'fail OPEN on ambiguity. A resolver only reports "not producible" for a shape it positively understands ... A false drop silently shrinks a site; a false keep ships one more empty page of a class we now detect downstream — the asymmetry decides.' This gate keeps that for INFRASTRUCTURE failures but treats an EMPTY tool set as a positive answer, because unlike the listing family there is no unknown-shape middle ground: a tool page's item source is one positively-understood thing.

builder_routing.go unavailableBuilders: `"tool": "tool-builder"` — the estate's existing capability_gap slug and item_key shape for a tool page with no builder, which this gate reuses so the two paths co-dedup rather than filing two rows for one page.

Council verdict on the sibling door half (corr 2b236e83, APPROVED 2026-09-03), architecture seat: 'The SQL predicate stays derived rather than stored, which is the correct answer to the future load I'd worry about: sites will keep arriving via the ~3h design rotation faster than plans stabilize.' The same rotation-vs-plan race is what this gate addresses on the supply side.
plan.risks: 1) THE §7 MEASUREMENT IS THE SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE. If anything ever DOES read planned tool pages to decide what to build, this gate starves that producer — the exact deadlock the 444 session warned about. It was measured at the rows on 2026-09-03 (tool-deployer creates its own rows; names disjoint; no reader found) and is stated in the file header as the thing to re-check if the gate misbehaves, but it is a NEGATIVE finding about consumers and negative findings go stale by addition. A reviewer who knows of such a reader should say so; the honest kill-switch is the key itself (default OFF, one jsonb_set to disarm). 2) ORDERING WITH THE LISTING GATE IS NEW BEHAVIOUR, not just placement: a /tools/ hub that would previously have been planned (children present) can now be held (children removed first). That is intended — an empty hub is a 444-class page — and it self-heals on the next replan once real tools exist, but it means arming this key changes what the LISTING gate does on the same plan. Pinned by a composition test; worth a reviewer's eye on whether any site legitimately wants a tools hub with no tools. 3) ADOPTED SITES: a ported tool living inline in a non-tool-level component makes its page resolve unproducible, so on a replan such a page is KEPT by the preserve guard (it is realised) but collects a spurious capability_gap receipt. Bounded, deduped, and the page is never harmed — but it is receipt noise on adopted estates and is stated rather than discovered later. 4) THE CENSUS IS SITE-SCOPED AND LIBRARY TOOLS DO NOT COUNT. A site whose tool exists only in the library, undeployed, has its page held. That is deliberate (§7: nothing consumes planned tool pages, so a library match would keep a page nothing will fill) but it is the arm most likely to surprise someone who thinks in terms of the component library. 5) WFA-013: `enforce_tool_sources` is a NINTH optional key on validate_site_plan, which has NO ActionInputSpec, so it is invisible to the optional-key budget exactly as the eight before it. No cron literal to keep in step — verified, cmd/config-key-audit has no reference to this action. The duty is declarative and this submission is it: BLD-028's verify-later (2) now has a second key strengthening the case for adopting a spec. 6) NOT ADDRESSED, deliberately: the existing 61-page shell population (realised; instance work), the owned_page_review hold's continuing lack of a consumer, and the migration that arms this key is a SEPARATE artefact reviewed on its own — this submission is the Go half, which is inert until a live row names the key.
